Quality Cost





                                       ME3327E QUALITY, RELIABILITY AND

Measuring Quality Costs

• The magnitude of quality costs is important to management because
  such indices as return on investment are calculated from it.
• For comparing quality costs over time, magnitude may not be the
 measure to use because conditions often change from one quarter to
  the next.
• The number of units produced may change, which affects the direct
  costs of labor and materials, so the total cost in Rupees/dollars may
  not be comparable.
• To alleviate this situation, a measurement base that accounts for
  labor hours, manufacturing costs, sales Rupees/dollars, or units
  produced could be used to produce an index.
     • Labor-based index
     • Cost-based index
     • Sales-based index
     • Unit-based index

Exercise

A medical industry manufacturer of blood filtration products, used in
dialysis, has to meet rigid standards in the field. Product design,
precision manufacturing equipment, and raw material/component
quality from suppliers are all important. Product failure at the customer
level is quite expensive and could cost ₹ 25,00,000 for each occurrence.
Yearly expenditures for the past year are shown in Table 3. Analyze the
various quality cost components. What proportion are they of total
quality costs? Find the total quality cost as a proportion of
manufacturing costs and sales and comment. Should senior
management stress less on design issues?

units.text:
Quality Function Deployment

• QFD is a planning tool that focuses on designing quality into a product
  or service by incorporating customer needs.
• It is a systems approach involving cross-functional teams (whose
 members are not necessarily from product design) that looks at the
  complete cycle of product development.
• This quality cycle starts with creating a design that meets customer
  needs and continues on through conducting detailed product
  analyses of parts and components to achieve the desired product,
  identifying the processes necessary to make the product, developing
  product requirements, prototype testing, final product or service
  testing, and finishing with after-sales troubleshooting.
• QFD reduces the product development cycle time in each functional area,
  from product inception and definition to production and sales.

             ME3327E QUALITY, RELIABILITY AND

Quality Loss Function

• The Quality Loss Function can be defined as a mathematical model
  that measures the financial loss incurred due to deviations from
  customer requirements or specifications.
• The function takes into account factors such as customer
  dissatisfaction, rework costs, warranty claims, and lost sales
  opportunities.
• The relevance of the Quality Loss Function in Quality Management is
  evident in its ability to identify areas where improvements can be
 made to reduce defects and enhance customer satisfaction.
• By understanding the financial implications of quality issues,
  organizations can prioritize their efforts and allocate resources
  effectively to address the most critical areas of concern.

units.text:
Significance of quality loss function

• It helps organizations to identify the root causes of quality defects
 and take appropriate corrective actions.
• It enables organizations to set quality targets and measure their
  progress towards achieving them.
• It provides a common language for communication within the
  organization and with external stakeholders.
• It serves as a valuable tool for Quality Management businesses to
  drive continuous improvement, enhance customer satisfaction, and
  reduce costs associated with quality defects.

units.text:
Benefits from quality loss function

• Organizations: By implementing the Quality Loss Function,
  organizations can identify areas of improvement, reduce defects, and
  ultimately enhance customer satisfaction.
• Customers: The Quality Loss Function helps organizations prioritize
  customer requirements and ensure that products or services meet
  their expectations.
• Employees: By reducing quality defects, organizations create a better
  working environment for employees.
• Suppliers: The Quality Loss Function encourages collaboration and
  communication between organizations and their suppliers.
• Shareholders: Shareholders benefit from the implementation of the
  Quality Loss Function through increased profitability and improved
  return on investment.

units.text:
Best practices

• Data Collection and Analysis: Organizations should establish robust
  data collection processes to gather relevant information on quality
  defects, customer complaints, and other quality-related metrics.
• Cross-functional Collaboration: Quality Management is a cross-
  functional endeavor that requires collaboration between different
  departments and stakeholders.
• Continuous Improvement: The Quality Loss Function should be
  viewed as a continuous improvement tool.
• Supplier Engagement: Organizations should involve their suppliers in
  quality improvement efforts.
• Leadership Support: Top management support is critical for the
  successful implementation of the Quality Loss Function.

Product Control Model

• Product control is another method of statistical quality control in
  which the quality of a product is controlled while the product is ready
  to dispatch or sell to the customers. Product control used the
  technique of acceptance sampling to detect defects and control the
  quality of a product.
